brandbook.positioning: App ficticia de ejemplo de Esteban para ajustar una única receta doméstica con cantidades claras, respuesta inmediata y preferencias guardadas solo en el navegador. Una herramienta cotidiana, no una marca comercial de alimentación.
brandbook.voice: Español breve, sobrio y práctico. Etiquetas directas, cantidades legibles y errores concretos con recuperación visible. Sin promesas comerciales, tecnicismos innecesarios ni celebraciones de guardado.
brandbook.motif: Dos medidas proporcionales y una marca lateral de resultado. La proporción pertenece al símbolo y la marca agrupa las tres cantidades de la ficha; no se extiende a ornamentos, patrones de fondo ni ilustraciones.

pages.title: Defining
pages.summary: Describe Porciones through its exact task: scaling one taco recipe from 1 to 20 people. Never imply a recipe catalog, nutrition service or shopping platform.

examples.title: Ajusta la receta a tu mesa
examples.text: Elige cuántas personas sois y consulta las cantidades de tortillas, carne y cebolla.

examples.title: Scope in one line
examples.text: Una calculadora para ajustar una receta de tacos.

pages.title: Vision & Mission
pages.summary: Use the supplied task as a project purpose, not an invented corporate mission. State what users can adjust and what the interface should make clear.

examples.title: Project purpose
examples.text: Make the relationship between people and ingredient quantities easy to read.

examples.title: Elige personas y unidades
examples.text: Ajusta entre 1 y 20 personas. Consulta carne y cebolla en gramos o kilogramos.

pages.title: Brand Values
pages.summary: Treat clarity, restraint and honest feedback as design criteria, not corporate claims. Each criterion must produce a visible interface choice.

examples.title: Clarity
examples.text: Show “400 gramos de carne” rather than an unexplained “400”.

examples.title: Restraint
examples.text: Keep one Tacos sheet, three ingredient rows and the controls needed to adjust them.

examples.title: Honest feedback
examples.text: Use “Preferencias guardadas en este navegador” only after a successful local write.

pages.title: Tone of Voice
pages.summary: Write interface copy in concise Spanish. Name the action or problem directly, then offer recovery. Avoid praise, sales language and technical explanations.

examples.title: Action
examples.text: Abrir calculadora

examples.title: Correction
examples.text: Introduce un número entero, sin decimales

examples.title: Recovery

pages.title: Logo
pages.summary: Introduce the identity with one lockup on white. The symbol expresses proportion; the separately typeset name provides recognition. Do not add a slogan inside the logo.

examples.title: Porciones
examples.text: Use the two open measures to the left of the name, with no enclosing badge.

pages.title: Logo overview
pages.summary: The symbol contains two open measures with equal wall thickness and a shared baseline. Their outer heights are 48 and 96 units, making the ratio visibly 1:2.

examples.title: Proportional construction
examples.text: Both measures are 40 units wide with 8-unit walls. Keep the supplied 160 × 160 viewBox unchanged.

examples.title: Header identification
examples.text: Pair the symbol with Porciones; place “App ficticia de ejemplo de Esteban” outside the lockup.

pages.title: Primary logo
pages.summary: Set Porciones in IBM Plex Sans 600, mixed case and natural tracking. Use a 32 px symbol canvas, an 8 px gap and a 20 px name in the compact header.

examples.title: Light header
examples.text: Measured Green symbol, Deep Olive name and Quiet Paper background.

examples.title: Dark presentation
examples.text: Keep the green symbol on a Quiet Paper support square; set Porciones in white beside it.

pages.title: Logo Safezone
pages.summary: Reserve clear space equal to one quarter of the symbol canvas around the complete lockup. Measure from visible letter edges and the symbol canvas, not a surrounding card.

examples.title: Compact header
examples.text: A 32 px symbol requires at least 8 px clear space around the combined symbol and name.

examples.title: Presentation sheet
examples.text: An 80 px symbol requires at least 20 px clear space. Keep captions beyond that boundary.

pages.title: Color combinations
pages.summary: Keep the symbol Measured Green #365C2A. On green or dark fields, add a Quiet Paper support surface rather than recoloring, outlining or dropping parts of the mark.

examples.title: White study
examples.text: #365C2A symbol and #20291F name on #FFFFFF.

examples.title: Green divider
examples.text: #FFFFFF name on #365C2A; the complete green symbol sits on #F7F8F4.

examples.title: Deep Olive cover
examples.text: #FFFFFF name on #20291F; retain the same light support behind the symbol.

pages.title: Brandmark
pages.summary: Use the symbol alone only where the surrounding context identifies Porciones. Reuse the exact geometry for icons; never replace the measures with a letter P or cooking illustration.

examples.title: Browser icon
examples.text: Center the two green measures on Quiet Paper and preserve the original canvas proportions.

examples.title: Small display
examples.text: At 16 px, retain both open tops and their common baseline. Do not add ticks or labels.

pages.title: Logo misuse
pages.summary: Do not stretch, rotate, round or decorate the measures. Preserve their 1:2 height relationship and keep the name in real typography rather than embedding it in the SVG.

examples.title: Avoid equal heights
examples.text: Making both measures the same height removes the proportional idea that identifies Porciones.

examples.title: Avoid culinary decoration
examples.text: Do not add tacos, leaves, steam or utensil silhouettes to the symbol.

examples.title: Avoid invented lettering
examples.text: Use “Porciones”, not “PORCIONES”, a script signature or a custom outlined wordmark.

pages.title: Typography
pages.summary: Let typography carry the interface. Use IBM Plex Sans throughout, with clear size changes and ample separation instead of decorative display lettering.

examples.title: Ajusta la receta a tu mesa
examples.text: Elige las personas y consulta las cantidades.

pages.title: Typography overview
pages.summary: Use one family for headings, controls, messages and quantities. Left-align text and preserve Spanish accents. Enable tabular figures for stable ingredient columns.

examples.title: Tacos · 4 personas
examples.text: 8 tortillas · 400 gramos de carne · 100 gramos de cebolla

examples.title: Stable quantities
examples.text: Keep number columns aligned when 400 changes to 2000; do not animate digits or center each row independently.

pages.title: Primary typeface
pages.summary: IBM Plex Sans is the specified family; supplied real font files include 400, 500, 600 and 700. Use 400–600 in the app. A system sans fallback is temporary, not the brand typeface.

examples.title: Calculadora
examples.text: Ajusta las cantidades de la receta de tacos.

examples.title: Family consistency
examples.text: Use IBM Plex Sans for the Porciones name, Personas input, unit options and local-storage messages.

pages.title: Typography styles
pages.summary: Use 400 for body copy and inputs, 500 for labels and buttons, and 600 for the name and UI headings. Reserve 700 for manual headings if needed; avoid italic status messages.

examples.title: Personas
examples.text: Introduce un número entero entre 1 y 20.

examples.title: Weight specimen
examples.text: Porciones: 600. Calculadora: 600. Restablecer: 500. Ingredient quantities and explanations: 400.

examples.title: Style restraint
examples.text: Keep “Último cálculo válido: 4 personas” upright and readable, not italic or all caps.

pages.title: Supporting type
pages.summary: Supporting text stays in IBM Plex Sans at 14 px with comfortable line spacing. Use Deep Olive for small copy; Sage Edge is a border token, not a small-text color.

examples.title: App ficticia de ejemplo de Esteban
examples.text: Una calculadora doméstica para ajustar una receta de tacos.

examples.title: Secondary does not mean faint
examples.text: Show “Preferencias recuperadas de este navegador” at 14 px in #20291F, without lowering opacity.

pages.title: Hierarchy
pages.summary: Set page titles at 32–40 px on desktop and 28 px on mobile. Use 16 px body text and inputs, 14 px buttons and secondary text. Keep one clear page title.

examples.title: Ajusta la receta a tu mesa
examples.text: Elige las personas y cambia entre gramos y kilogramos.

examples.title: Sheet hierarchy
examples.text: Page title first, then “Tacos”, then “Personas” and the unit group. Quantities remain prominent without becoming extra headings.

pages.title: Layouts
pages.summary: Build one aligned recipe sheet using 8, 12, 16, 24 and 32 px spacing. At 768 px, stack controls above results. Use 4 px corners and borders rather than floating card effects.

examples.title: Tacos
examples.text: Personas · Unidad para carne y cebolla · Cantidades

examples.title: Desktop composition
examples.text: Connect left-hand controls to right-hand results. Keep status and Restablecer on the sheet’s lower edge.

examples.title: 390 × 600 composition
examples.text: Use a 56 px header and compact vertical rhythm. Fit the valid flow without fixed-height clipping; let errors extend the document.

pages.title: Colors
pages.summary: Use Measured Green for this divider and white for its short title. Across the interface, light surfaces dominate; green identifies action and focus rather than decoration.

examples.title: Porciones
examples.text: Clear quantities. Quiet surfaces. One measured accent.

pages.title: Colors overview
pages.summary: Preserve all supplied hex values. Assign each color a fixed role; add #A12622 only for errors. Color must reinforce labels and states, never replace their meaning.

examples.title: Foundation
examples.text: Quiet Paper #F7F8F4: page. Clear Sheet #FFFFFF: recipe surface. Deep Olive #20291F: headings, body and quantities.

examples.title: Interaction
examples.text: Measured Green #365C2A: primary action and focus. Sage Edge #778373: borders, not small text. Keep editable boundaries at least 3:1.

examples.title: Correction
examples.text: Error #A12622: invalid field border and message. Pair it with “El mínimo es 1 persona”, not color alone.

pages.title: Using Tints
pages.summary: Keep text, focus and control boundaries solid. Reserve opacity changes for the lateral result marker. Do not create pastel status colors or fade text to suggest hierarchy.

examples.title: Result marker
examples.text: After a valid adjustment, reveal #365C2A through opacity over 160 ms while the quantities update immediately.

examples.title: Disabled control
examples.text: At 1 person, disable the minus action clearly; keep its shape and focus-independent meaning recognizable.

pages.title: Graphic Elements
pages.summary: Limit the graphic vocabulary to the proportional symbol and one lateral marker beside the three result rows. Reserve marker space so valid updates never shift the sheet.

examples.title: Three rows, one marker
examples.text: Group “8 tortillas”, “400 gramos de carne” and “100 gramos de cebolla” with a single vertical green accent.

examples.title: Motion restraint
examples.text: Use a 160 ms opacity transition only after valid changes. Reduced motion shows the final state directly; invalid edits do not reactivate it.

pages.title: Icons
pages.summary: Use simple functional icons only where they clarify a control. Match visual weight to the UI, preserve 44 px targets and keep visible labels for recovery actions.

examples.title: Restablecer
examples.text: Vuelve a 4 personas y gramos.

examples.title: Stepper names
examples.text: Give minus and plus the accessible names “Restar una persona” and “Sumar una persona”.

examples.title: Icon restraint
examples.text: Do not add ingredient emoji or utensil icons. The three ingredient names already identify the results.

pages.title: Photography
pages.summary: Do not use photography in this identity. The recipe sheet is the product showcase; images would compete with the quantities and the compact mobile flow.

examples.title: Inicio showcase
examples.text: Present “Tacos · 4 personas” with its three quantities instead of a taco photograph.

examples.title: Presentation material
examples.text: Use a clean crop of the designed recipe sheet on Quiet Paper, not a kitchen scene or stock-food backdrop.

pages.title: Moodboard
pages.summary: Build the visual reference from proportion sheets, tabular numbers and quiet surfaces. Reject illustrated notebooks, radial scales and commercial food-page conventions.

examples.title: Chosen direction
examples.text: A white Tacos sheet, olive text, thin sage borders and a green adjustment marker.

examples.title: Excluded direction
examples.text: No illustrated ingredients, circular serving dial, promotional hero or repeated feature cards.

pages.title: Applications
pages.summary: Design studies translate the same sheet, alignment and voice across formats. They do not add app routes, products or services. Keep Porciones recognizable through structure, not decoration.

examples.title: Porciones
examples.text: Ajusta la receta a tu mesa.

examples.title: Shared composition
examples.text: Use a compact lockup, one task-led headline and a three-row quantity block. Avoid adding promotional sections to fill space.

pages.title: Social media icons

examples.title: Avatar crop

pages.title: Social media profiles

pages.title: Posters

pages.title: T shirts and totes
pages.summary: Design study: use a small lockup on a plain light textile. Keep the mark flat and proportional; do not introduce a merchandise range, price or purchase call to action.

examples.title: Print placement
examples.text: Use Measured Green for the symbol and Deep Olive for the name on a light panel. Keep surrounding space greater than the logo safezone.

pages.title: Recipe sheet sleeve
pages.summary: Design study: adapt packaging to a sleeve for a printed recipe reference, not takeaway food. Place the name on the front and keep recipe information on the enclosed sheet.

examples.text: Use a white sleeve with a small green symbol and Deep Olive title. No food-safety seals, delivery labels or product claims.

pages.summary: Design study: the entry point is the lower edge of the Inicio recipe sheet, not a physical pickup location. Keep its action visually attached to the example it opens.

pages.title: Portion controls
pages.summary: Design study: place Personas before the unit radios. Use visible labels, 44 px targets and green focus rings. Invalid input keeps its literal text and blocks steppers and unit changes.

examples.text: Gramos · Kilogramos

examples.title: Range and validation
examples.text: Use “Introduce el número de personas” for empty input and “El máximo es 20 personas” above the limit. Keep Restablecer available.

examples.title: Keyboard behavior
examples.text: Tab reaches each action; arrow keys change unit radios. Disable minus at 1 and plus at 20 without changing the control layout.

pages.title: Quantity summary
pages.summary: Design study: replace receipt conventions with three live ingredient rows. Show quantities and units, never totals, order numbers or confirmation of a transaction.

examples.title: Retained result
examples.text: On invalid input, label the unchanged quantities “Último cálculo válido: 4 personas”. Retain their previous unit and do not animate them.

pages.title: Preference reminder
pages.summary: Design study: replace rewards language with a quiet browser-preference note inside the existing sheet. Distinguish recovery from saving; imply no account, membership or cloud storage.

examples.text: Se conservarán al recargar mientras este navegador permita el almacenamiento local.

examples.title: State placement
examples.text: Keep the note beside recovery actions at the sheet’s lower edge. Initial defaults and recovered values must not be presented as a new save.

pages.title: Demo display sign
pages.summary: Design study: adapt signage to a project demonstration, not a restaurant. Lead with Porciones and a short task description; omit addresses, opening hours and service claims.

examples.text: Calculadora de cantidades para una receta de tacos.

examples.title: Display treatment
examples.text: Use white lettering on Deep Olive. Keep the green symbol on its Quiet Paper support and place the fictional-project credit below.

pages.summary: Design study: use exactly / and /calculadora. Keep Inicio and Calculadora visible in the shared header, including on mobile. No login, payments, email forms, database or extra sections.

examples.title: Inicio · Calculadora
examples.text: Indicate the current page without hiding either link. Preserve native navigation and history; do not redirect Inicio automatically.

examples.title: Quiet interface
examples.text: Adapt shadcn/ui controls to the single sheet. Configured Constructor Analytics and Views add no promotional panels or preference-sharing copy.

pages.title: Favicon
pages.summary: Design study: derive the browser and application icons from the exact supplied symbol geometry. Use a Quiet Paper background so both green measures remain visible in light and dark chrome.

examples.title: Porciones
examples.text: Calculadora de recetas.

examples.title: Small-scale identity
examples.text: Use the same two open measures in app/icon.svg and other icon sizes. Do not replace them with a template icon, letter or filled cup.

pages.title: Stationery
pages.summary: Design study: treat stationery as a project note sheet. Align the lockup, title and body to one left edge; leave the lower area open rather than inventing contact details.

examples.text: Place a small lockup above the title. Use 16 px-equivalent body copy and a single Sage Edge rule, with no decorative background pattern.

pages.title: Project cards
pages.summary: Design study: adapt business cards to identify the fictional project and its author. Use a name-led front and a concise task description on the reverse; omit invented contact channels.

pages.title: Recipe reference card
pages.summary: Design study: replace a gift card with a non-monetary recipe reference. Show the base quantities clearly; include no value, redemption code, purchase message or extra app action.
